text:
mike (engineering): Draft of release notes and internal announce ready for quick eyes — targeting EU cutover window 03/27 02:00-04:00 UTC. Can folks check pinning/rollback language?

sara (product): Thanks — will scan now. do we have the canary thresholds documented?

ana (eng-sre): @mike quick nit: please call out exact model and infra pins. e.g. pinned model: redwood/llm-3b@v1.4.2, infra: dedicated-gpu-pool-7.

mike (engineering): good call. adding: "Pinned model: redwood/llm-3b@v1.4.2 (quantized-INT4), Fallback: redwood/llm-3b@v1.4.1"

elaine (docs): I'll tidy the release note bullets and internal blurb. can you paste the blurb you want in the internal announce? short paragraph is best.

sara (product): Blurb draft: "Internal: We’re rolling v1.4.2 which improves inference tail latency and reduces token-cost by ~12%. Canary in EU 03/27 02:00 UTC; fallback to v1.4.1 if error rate or service latency exceed thresholds."

daniel (oncall): What are the concrete thresholds? I need numbers for the oncall runbook.

mike (engineering): Proposed thresholds:
- Errors: >= 3% 5xx or malformed outputs over 5m window -> trigger rollback
- Latency: p95 > 700ms for 10m rolling -> scale back / rollback decision
- Quality regression: automated eval score drop > 2% on canary prompt-set -> rollback

ana (eng-sre): I suggest we add an automatic canary limit: stop canary and roll back if failed shards > 1 or GPU OOM rate > 0.5% across pool. Also set traffic cap to 5% user traffic initially.

mike (engineering): agreed. canary config: 5% traffic for 30m, then 25% for 30m, then full. auto-abort if thresholds hit.

deploy-bot: Deploy job queued: job_id=deploy-1742105432-1, target=eu-dedicated-gpu-pool-7, model=redwood/llm-3b@v1.4.2

deploy-bot: Canary started — 5% traffic routing active. monitor dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/canary/1742105432

elaine (docs): Paste for internal announce (short):
"Heads-up: Rolling v1.4.2 to EU (canary 03/27 02:00 UTC). Improvements: lower tail latency, cost reductions. Canary will be staged; we have clear rollback thresholds. Oncall: @daniel, @ana. See internal canary dashboard for metrics."

sara (product): That reads well. add note: "Do not escalate to customers unless rollback occurs."

daniel (oncall): Copy. I'll prepare runbook snippet and a one-click rollback command in runbook. Suggested quick rollback command:
```
# rollback to pinned stable
deploy-bot rollback --job deploy-1742105432-1 --to redwood/llm-3b@v1.4.1
```

mike (engineering): added runbook note: if automated abort triggers, engineers get paged and deploy-bot will mark job aborted. manual rollback after investigation window (5m) unless P1.

ana (eng-sre): small request: can we add a short postmortem template link in the internal announce so folks know how to file?

elaine (docs): done — adding link to templates and a 1-paragraph summary section.

mike (engineering): final checklist before internal blast:
- [x] release notes draft (elaine)
- [x] pin & fallback declared (mike)
- [x] canary thresholds in runbook (daniel)
- [x] deploybot job queued (deploy-bot)
- [x] internal announce copy ready (sara/elaine)

sara (product): I'll send the internal announce T-30 minutes pre-cutover and ping eng-releases. Quick ask: anyone object to short embargo to keep external comms until feature metrics look good?

ana (eng-sre): no objections from infra. prefer embargo until 3rd stage full traffic.

daniel (oncall): oncall OK. I'll have the rollback command ready in pager message.

mike (engineering): launching final publish to internal channel at T-30. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary progress: 5% -> 5m: errors 0.4%, p95 310ms, GPU mem 78%

elaine (docs): Great numbers, will update the internal thread after 30m check.

sara (product): I'll wait for 30m checkpoint then push external note draft to comms if stable.

mike (engineering): ok closing thread — will post checkpoint update in 30m.
